title: Allowed moves
plain: First decide what changes are legal. Without that rule, no invariant means anything.

title: Invariant receipts
plain: An invariant is a receipt for what survived the trip from one picture to another.

title: Holes and boundaries
plain: Holes are not empty decoration; they are missing routes, blocked fillings, and accounting terms.

title: Curves, loops, and knots
plain: A loop can carry memory of how it sits in space, even when its exact length and shape are forgotten.

title: Turning and curvature
plain: Curvature is a way of measuring how direction changes, and totals often matter more than point-by-point values.

title: Signs and cancellation
plain: Opposite contributions can be born or die together while the total stays fixed.

title: Surfaces and orientation
plain: A surface may have two sides, one side, a boundary, or no boundary, and those facts govern what can be drawn on it.

title: Mechanisms and locks
plain: Some physical systems are explained by the routes their parts are allowed to take.

title: Singular moments
plain: A special accident is often the moment where two ordinary pictures meet.

title: Models, not labels
plain: The course's named ideas matter only when they help build a usable mental model.
